newsitem.title: EGYPT: Ross says negotiations now on non-Hebron issues.
newsitem.headline: Ross says negotiations now on non-Hebron issues.

text.p: A U.S. envoy to the Middle East said on Saturday the Israeli and Palestinian sides had "basically" resolved the issue of Israel's withdrawal from the West Bank town of Hebron but that other problems remained.
Middle East peace mediator Dennis Ross said he told Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak during their meeting earlier in the day that "we basically have resolved the Hebron issue".
"We achieved a great deal of progress...but we have not overcome all the differences yet," Ross told reporters before leaving to the foreign ministry.
U.S. officials say Ross has all but sewn up the Hebron part of the deal but that Palestinians have turned down a U.S. compromise date of 1998 for completing further West Bank withdrawals.
"We are working with the two sides to see if we can find and develop the kind of common ground that would permit us to come to a conclusion," said Ross.
"We made a lot of progress on the Hebron issues and we still have gaps on some of the non-Hebron issues," he said.

Palestinian-Israeli talks on an Israeli pullout from 80 percent of Hebron have been deadlocked over the Palestinians' insistence that Israel adhere to a 1995 interim peace deal that requires withdrawal from various other parts of the West Bank by September 1997.
Mubarak has just ended a separate meeting with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, who arrived in Cairo on Saturday, before the arrival of Ross at the presidential palace.
Arafat, who left to Gaza after the meeting, pays regular visits to Egypt to brief Mubarak on latest developments in the peace talks.
Ross is also expected to meet the Palestinian senior official, Saeb Erekat, in a bid to overcome remaining differences between the Israelis and Palestinians.
The Palestinians and Israelis admit the problem now has less to do with Hebron than with three further transfers of West Bank areas to Palestinian control.
When Ross was asked whether he would meet Arafat in Gaza he said no time has been set but added he expected to see the Palestinian leader "at some point".
Ross added he would return to Israel after his visit to Cairo.
